title: Divrei Chalomot
text:
Monday night, Parashat Bo, the second of Shevat. I dreamed about what they said in Sanhedrin (65b) "He said to him: return to your dust," from which was derived in the responsa of Chakham Tzvi (§93) that it [[a golem]] does not have the benefit of being included for a davar shebikedusha [[counted in a minyan]]. This is not necessarily so, because we could say that he feared that it would become injurious to humanity when it grew a little bit, and then even the one who made it would find it difficult to return it to its dust, because it could also injure him, and as told in the Sheilat Yaavetz Part II (§82) about the one created by his ancestor, our teacher Rabbi Eliyahu Baal Shem. And therefore, one should not maintain a creation like that, but create it for a purpose for which it is needed [for surely he sent it before Rabbi Zeira was for some particular hidden need that was not explained in the Talmud, for which the necessity was to send in this way a creation like this], and then to return it immediately afterward to its dust. And for that reason they said there afterward about Rabbi Haninah and Rabbi Oshaya, who created a third-grown calf, that it was Sabbath eve. And in the responsum of Rashba (§413) investigated this and wrote a reason, and we can say that this too is in the category of miraculous acts that it is forbidden to get benefit from them, as in Taanit (24b) — only for the purpose of a mitzvah [[commandment]] can we say that it is permitted. And they were poor, because they are Rav Haninah and Rav Oshaya who are mentioned in Chapter "Arvei Pesachim" [[Chapter 10 of tractate Pesachim]] (top of 113b) who were cobblers, not the Rabbi Haninah and Rabbi Oshaya the students of Rabbi (and see Korban Minha of the Mahari Hagiz, end of §395) and they were lacking the needs of Shabbat and they ate it in a Shabbat meal, and that is why they made it on Shabbat eve [and in any case any preparation for Shabbat should be done Shabbat eve as is written on Friday, when they prepared (Exodus 15:6), and as is known], because if they did it earlier, it would grow until Shabbat and become injurious, and they would need to return it to its dust. And it seemed to me that they also would need to make a blemish on it earlier, so that it would not be suitable for a sacrifice, because if not, it could not be returned to its dust because it has a use, that it is suitable for sacrificing [thus it seemed to me in my dream simply that it was suitable for sacrificing, and if it was so, there is maybe some reason, while the Temple is standing, however, because it could be sacrificed, to forbid returning it to its dust because of bal tashchit [[not wasting]], because it is suitable for some thing, and as it was simply in my eyes in my dream. Except that if so, making a blemish would also be forbidden — one should only sacrifice it. But the truth seems to me now straightforward, that this is among the nonsensical features that always appear in dreams [[lit. one cannot dream without them]], for surely it was disqualified for sacrifice, as it is written when is born (Leviticus 22:27) and the ruling is that we exclude a cesarean section based on that phrase — all the more so this, which was not born from a mother's womb at all. And all the more so because of what the Shelah [[Isaiah ben Avraham Ha-Levi Horowitz]] wrote in Parashat Vayeshev that it doesn't need ritual slaughter, and see there also that it doesn't have prohibitions on forbidden fat or blood, see there. And perforce it must be that it is not offered on the altar. About the essence of the Chakham Tzvi's ruling, it seems to me that the insight I mentioned is valid. And in my dream it seemed to me that the straightforward ruling should not be like him, and that it is suitable for a davar shebikedusha [[counted in a minyan]].

And it seems that it is possible to maintain this and what is written in Sheilat Yaavetz there that it [[a golem]] is not preferable to a deafmute who neither hears nor speaks, and so it is in Barchei Yosef Orach Chayim §55. This is not necessarily so, because a deafmute is not bar da'at [[is not a rational being/does not have a mind]], like a child, because a person is created without da'at, only one gets da'at when one grows up. And one who neither hears nor speaks, whether from birth, because they don't learn da'at from people, or whether they become deaf afterward, they don't have da'at because a deficiency emerged in their brain. But this one, who was created full-sized as an adult person, we might say that it also has da'at like an adult, and even though it neither hears nor speaks, we might say that it is not from a deficiency in its brain and da'at, and that it would not have a da'at.

And even though it is written in Chesed leAvraham, Ein Yaakov, Stream 30 that it does not have a soul or a speaking spirit, only an animalistic spirit, and therefore one is permitted to kill it like an animal, see there, and so it is in the Maharsha in Part 1 in Sanhedrin there — we can say that it is not like an animal in the shape of a person, because after all, it was created with Sefer Yetzira in the way to make a person, and not in the way to make an animal. But the living soul of blew into his mouth (Genesis 2:7), which is the ruach memalelah [[speaking spirit]], because it is the divine part from above, that we annot put into it. But in any case, it is not worse than an idolater, who also does not have the divine part from above, and even though they can speak, that is in their tongue, and that is not called speech. For about that they said (Midrash Rabbah Balak) that an idolater who speaks in the holy tongue, their language is putrid, because they do not have a true speaking spirit, just like the chirping of birds and like the snake before the sin who could speak even though it did not have a living soul, and this is from the sitra achra [[the demonic forces, lit. the "other side"]] and the stature of a worthless person. And this one, that was created in holiness with the Sefer Yetzirah, we cannot put speech into it from the side of the sitra achra, and the speaking spirit of the holiness we also can't, and therefore it does not speak [and according to this, we might say that it could hear, and not like the simple understanding]. And if so, it is comparable to an idolater rather than an animal. And even if you say that one is permitted to kill a Noahide and one is not killed over them — we can say from the decree of the verse a person in/for a person, as written in the responsa of Chakham Tzvi there, but in any case for the matter of da'at, it is fair to say that it [[a golem]] has it, just as we call an idolater bar da'at, rather that "they act according to their own da'at," as they said in Gittin 23a. And we cannot say that da'at always depends on speech and the idolater, just as their speech is from the side of the kelipah, so to their da'at, and that is the meaning of "they act according to their own da'at," and their da'at is not effective for the purposes of a writ of divorce or a matter of mitzvah <commandment>, and a golem, as it doesn't have speech for the reasons mentioned, so too it doesn't have da'at. For this cannot be, because after all, there in Gittin, Rashi explained "lest, perhaps...", so only because of doubt do we disqualify their da'at for a writ of divorce. And the Tosafot wrote there that their da'at is stam [[indeterminate, neutral]], and therefore they are permissible for circumcision, even though that needs to be with the right intention, see there. Furthermore, da'at is not at all dependent solely on speech, for after all, a mute person has da'at, and even a mute person from birth, it could be that they can hear, and if so, it could be that this is also a bar da'at.

However, we can say for a different reason, that in any case, it [[a golem]] is not obligated in the commandments, and if so, even if you say that we can call it a member of Israel, for the reason the Chakham Tzvi says there, that it is the handiwork of the a tzadik [[righteous person]], in any case it would seem that we cannot obligate it in the commandments for this reason and say that everything written in the Torah speak to the people of Israel, it [[a golem]] will also be included, because it does not have a living soul or the continuation of the soul into the next world for reward and punishment. If so, how could we include it for a davar shebikedusha [[count it in a minyan]] because it is not obligated. And we can say in any case for the matter of ten for birchat hamazon [[grace after meals]], if it can eat, for we include a child, that we include it too, and it is also possible that it knows Whom we are blessing. And it requries more clarification, and this is not the place to extend the discussion.

Saturday evening after Shabbat Beshalach, I was doubtful about a dream. It was about what is in Yevamot 37a, the doubt of whether a child is a 9-month baby to the first husband or a 7-month baby to the levir, for one child would be kosher and the other a doubtful mamzer. Since we see that the first baby is modest and excellent, and the second is known by its blossoming and by its sins from its suckling era, that it is brazen like many mamzerim, who are rebels and sinners. If we rely on this ruling to establish a chazaka, for the child to be like a certain mamzer. And logically, it seems simple that we don't rely, since there are many brazen in the world who are not mamzerim, and "at the footsteps of Mashach, cheek will be common", and therefore many wicked will be wicked from the womb. And although they are sons of one father and mother, if the first is the child of the levir, Ya'akov and Esav struggled and were twins! And the sons of totally righteous parents! And all the more so, those who are not twins and are the children of general people. And perhaps the second is a of the nine attributes mentioned in Nedarim 20b, etc. Rather, it's proper to pay attention to the fact of Rabbi Bena'ah in Bava Batra 58a, who relied on an experiment to establish the brazen as mamzerim even in a case of money. And it's necessary to say, even though in a case of money we don't go after a chazaka, that's only to remove money from a chazaka. Rather, one can say that it's certain that nine of the sons were mamzerim, so there's certainly a mamzer present. And without this, the father willed that the one would inherit and didn't specify who, so against your will you have to submit to the wisdom of the beit din who will clarify the matter with their wisdom. One can also say that Ketubot 85b is similar to this, where someone willed their possessions to Toviyah and two Toviyahs came forwards, that the judges pay attention to the likelihood of the deceased's intent being to which one, see Rashi there. And I also saw the Rashbam wrote in Bava Batra as I wrote, see there, with this words to this one... that the beit din will explain... and these words said... and R Bena'ah judged well, that this is only appropriate for shuda [a case with two creditors only one of whom can be paid, where the beit din is able to select one of them to be paid]. But, when I did not know why I should follow after chariots, and brought proof for shuda dedaynei from the Ketubot which was mentioned earlier, according to which I first wrote that his intent was to whichever the beit din should select. If so, it's certain that the beit din should select accordng to their wisdom and logic, for they are not prophets to know who the deceased intended - and he himself did not know, and said it without explanation! It's impossible for anyone to know, and so the matter is handed over to the beit din. And those who informed on Rav Bena'ah and said that he was fining people without witnesses (Bava Batra 58a), were just saying lashon hara, for he didn't fine anyone! Behold, the father said clearly that only one should receive money - and the matter was weighed, and you must admit that he intended this. And with regard to Ketubot 85a, he knew which Toviyah he intended, but since one can say that he forgot and didn't conclude in his mind, thus his wealth goes to the other Toviyah - he needed to signal this and single him out, and there's no proof that he gave to the beit din! In any case, they said that this is shuda dedaynei and this is an expansion, which is necessary to teach us there. But here, where it is simple - for behold, the matter is surrendered to the beit din and they will clarify his words, as I have written. And it seems from this to prove the opposite - for if the matter wasn't shuda dedaynei then he would not have judged well, and we would not have relied on his estimate as discussed. And since one could say it's different there, where he is not so brazen, for behold Rav Bena'ah commanded them to do such [beat their father's grave] and they did so at the command of the beit din! And it's possible that even the kosher one would do this. And what was written at the start, with the dibbur hamatchil "chavoto", that mamzerim are brazen and will beat it, there it is certain that they will do it, but the kasher will perhaps not wish to even though he is commanded, and so we can rely on this, as it is just shuda and not a true estimate.
